summary: The control plane can now run a video wall that spans recorders. Pick cameras from any appliance in the fleet, arrange them in a grid, give the wall a name, and it is saved centrally — the same wall for everybody who opens the screen, rather than something each person rebuilds in their own browser at the start of every shift. It rotates through its pages on its own if you ask it to, and one wall can be marked the one a screen opens with. The part a single recorder cannot do at all: when a camera on the wall raises an alert, the wall shows that camera and stops rotating until you have had time to look — and the alert can come from any building, because this is the only thing that sees all of them. Tiles are honest about what they cannot show: a camera on an appliance that is offline says so in words instead of going black, which matters because a black rectangle looks exactly like a dark room, and one on an appliance that has left the fleet says that instead, because they are different problems. A tile is never quietly dropped from an arrangement.
compatibility: Additive: the existing Live Views page is untouched and still works as the scratchpad it always was. Anybody who can see the fleet can watch a wall; building and changing one is administrator-only, because a wall is shared — changing it changes what everybody on that screen sees, including whoever is mid-shift and did not change anything — and because the default wall decides what a guard station opens with. Two limits worth knowing. Every tile is a live stream relayed from another machine rather than decoded locally, so a wall is capped at 32 cameras and what your network can actually carry may be fewer; the screen says so where you are choosing. And a wall may name cameras on appliances a viewer could not otherwise browse, which is the other reason building one is an administrator's job.
